sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with \(P(A_i=1\mid X_i=x)=e(x)\) and fixed overlap \(\epsilon\le e\le1-\epsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: The overlap constant \(\epsilon\) is known to the test and does not vary with \(n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No fitted-nuisance rate is assumed; all signal and nuisance grid ranks and every calibration constant are functions only of \(n,d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4.2 defines \(s_P\) as the \(L^2(P_U)\) projection of the loss score onto \(\mathcal G_P\) and \(\xi_P\) as the hunted direction after projection off \(\mathcal F_P\); Corollary 2 gives power over \(\{P:\tau_P\ge\varepsilon_n\}\) when \(\operatorname{Corr}_P(s_P(U),\xi_P(U)\mid\widehat h)>\rho_n\) uniformly with high probability and \(n\rho_n^2\varepsilon_n\to\infty\).

Assumption 4 and Theorem 1 give asymptotic normality for the intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under separate \(o_P(n^{-1/4})\) propensity, outcome-regression, and CATE learner errors and a root-\(n\) ATE error.
Theorem 1 gives the pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate with a nuisance-smoothness elbow.
The main minimax theorems give phasewise heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under rough mean regression.
The paper derives sharp weighted U-tests and minimax constants for regression nulls defined by nonnegative quadratic functionals.
Theorem 1 gives rate-optimal quadratic U-tests for multivariate Gaussian regression under known random uniform design.
Theorem 4 gives a weighted chi-square null limit for a second-order U-statistic testing equality of unknown functions.
The spline specialization gives a minimax projected-covariance test under common smoothness and nondegeneracy conditions.
The paper constructs nonparametric tests for zero and constant conditional average treatment effects under unconfoundedness.

The paper gives an observational treatment-effect heterogeneity test based on propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistics that bypasses modeling the treatment effect in each study subgroup, with an asymptotic normality result.
The paper gives nonparametric quantitative and qualitative homogeneity tests with fixed and local asymptotic power analyses.
The paper gives boundary-robust confidence intervals for explained treatment-effect variance in randomized experiments.

body.tldr: Constant-CATE testing is posed over the explicit observed-data image of a full causal-law Hölder class, so potential-outcome identification and every minimax supremum now live at the correct levels. A separate oracle radius ranges over measurable tests of \((O^n,e_P)\). A coercive profiled moment and known-design product correction yield an explicit higher-order cross-energy test with candidate upper rate \(R_{\mathrm{up}}=n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\vee n^{-4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)/(4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)+d(\alpha+\beta)+2d\gamma)}\). The central open theorem remains the sharp same-image observational frontier. A risk-projection lemma derives the exact Dhawan--Guo--Shah score on \(U=(A,X)\), showing that its energy is equivalent to \(V(P)\) under overlap while its learner, variance, and direction-correlation restrictions remain additional; the companion phase map compares those restrictions and Yu's learner regime with the uniform minimax radius without claiming subsumption in advance.

project_justification.gap: Existing observational homogeneity tests document asymptotic size and power under learned-direction, learner-remainder, or multisample U-statistic conditions; existing Hölder theory treats CATE estimation, direct regression, conditional-mean independence under different classes, or heteroskedasticity rather than the declared constant-CATE experiment.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the full-class minimax separation radius when the null contains every unknown constant effect and arbitrary permitted rough propensity and baseline functions, including regimes in which both useful sieve ranks exceed sample size and first-order product conditions fail.
project_justification.fill: The project targets an algorithmic upper bound and matching observational converse on one unchanged statistical class through an exact full-law-to-observed-image bridge, a profiled bounded-weight score, deterministic local-polynomial product correction, independent higher-order cross-energy, and a null-preserving observed-likelihood mixture program; the risk-projection lemma places Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah on the phase map under their own conditions.

body.related_work: Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026), Section 3.1.1, formulate effect-modifier testing as identity-link conditional-mean risk minimization with generic predictor \(U=(A,X)\), an unrestricted-baseline null class, and ambient class \(L^2(P_U)\). Their Section 4.2 defines \(s_P\) as the \(L^2\) projection of the loss score and \(\xi_P\) as the hunted function minus its null-class projection; Corollary 2 requires their regularity and estimation conditions, conditional correlation above \(\rho_n\), and \(n\rho_n^2\varepsilon_n\to\infty\). The score-translation lemma derives, rather than assumes, that the constant-CATE specialization has \(s_P(U)=(A-e(X))(\bar\tau_w-\tau(X))\) and effect energy equivalent to \(V(P)\); it does not infer the required correlation or conditional score-variance bound from the Hölder class. Yu (2026), Assumption 4 and Theorem 1, directly targets CATE variance with intra-fold splitting under separate \(o_P(n^{-1/4})\) learner errors and a root-\(n\) ATE error, while its boundary-nondegeneracy condition is not imposed here. The open phase comparison therefore asks for legal sequences before asserting any non-subsumption. Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik (2008) provide the classical constant-CATE test. Dai, Shen and Stern (2023), Canadian Journal of Statistics 51(2):531--558, provide a propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistic test for observational treatment-effect heterogeneity that bypasses modeling the treatment effect in each study subgroup; they do not characterize the continuous Hölder minimax frontier. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (2024) supply the closest causal minimax geometry for pointwise CATE estimation. Kotekal and Kundu (2025), Annals of Statistics 53(1):295--321, give sharp heteroskedasticity-testing rates with a rough mean. Comminges and Dalalyan (2013), Ingster and Sapatinas (2009), Luedtke, Carone and van der Laan (2019), and Lundborg, Kim, Shah and Samworth (2024) inform the quadratic and projected-score constructions under different experiments. Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (2024) and Sánchez-Becerra (2023) study complementary homogeneity-inference targets rather than this full-class radius.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The displayed \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\) is an upper-envelope candidate. The presolve's coefficient-covariance bound, simultaneous profiling constants, and numerical basis constants still require complete proof. More importantly, the oracle lower bound proves no nuisance penalty and cannot certify \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\): at \(d=1\), \(\alpha=1/64\), \(\beta=9/64\), and \(\gamma=1/8\), a valid converse must preserve baseline smoothness while accounting for every transition region observed under uniform design. Failure of one mixture construction is not evidence that the nuisance exponent is false.
body.honest_scope: The target statistical class is exactly the observed image \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) of bounded full causal laws satisfying consistency, conditional exchangeability, exact uniform design, fixed strong overlap, and separate Hölder smoothness for \(e^{\mathrm F}\), \(\mu_0^{\mathrm F}\), and \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\). The observed-image lemma gives the equivalent observed-law restrictions, so minimax tests never receive latent variables. There is no uniform interior arm-mean or conditional-variance lower bound; the affine Bernoulli witness is interior only to provide lower-bound perturbation slack. The DGS comparison is restricted to laws also satisfying that paper's variance, estimation, nondegeneracy, and Lyapunov conditions, and the Yu comparison retains its boundary conditions; neither restriction is added to the minimax class. Unknown design density, smoothness adaptation, and outcomes outside \([0,1]\) are outside scope. The known-propensity benchmark and computable observational upper bound are theorem targets; the matching observational rate, individual smoothness dependence, boundary logarithms, and strict phasewise comparisons remain open. Under supplied propensity, the frontier must reduce to \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\).
